subject: CorpFlux GCP Private Offer — Onramp & Acceptance Plan
messages:
From: Anna Lee <anna@corpflux.io>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Menon <rajesh@corpflux.io>
Date: 2028-03-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: CorpFlux GCP Private Offer — next steps

Sergio / Kimberly,

Thanks for the walkthrough today. The execs liked the pricing shape but want a clear onramp timeline for the GCP private offer and a short MAP we can present to procurement. Key asks from our side:
- Acceptance criteria for technical sign-off (latency / throughput docs).
- Billing path for a marketplace private offer (invoice cadence, PO flow).
- Legal SOW draft to review.

Can you send a one-sheet MAP and an SOW draft by next Wednesday (4/4)? Procurement (cc'd) wants to start legal review immediately after.

— Anna
Anna Lee
Head of Platform Engineering, CorpFlux
anna@corpflux.io
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lee <anna@corpflux.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Rajesh Menon <rajesh@corpflux.io>
Date: 2028-03-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: CorpFlux GCP Private Offer — next steps

Anna — thanks, this is helpful. Attaching an initial MAP spreadsheet and a draft SOW for procurement's intake (see attachments). High level plan below, happy to adjust: 

1) Internal validation (week 0):
   - Redwood to provide performance profile and recommended model/quantization. Owner: Sergio. Deliverable: Performance PDF. Due: 4/1.
2) Staged onramp (week 1–2):
   - Sandbox private offer deployment in CorpFlux GCP project (RBAC + VPC peering). Owner: Kimberly. Deliverable: sandbox endpoint + low-volume acceptance tests. Due: 4/10.
3) Technical acceptance (week 3):
   - Acceptance tests: 95th perc latency < 320ms for sample load; KV cache hit verification; smoke tests for streaming. Owner: Lauren & CorpFlux engineering. Deliverable: acceptance checklist. Due: 4/17.
4) Billing & procurement (parallel):
   - Redwood issues invoice monthly to CorpFlux finance (Net 30) via GCP Private Offer pipeline. Procurement PO accepted via marketplace commitment. Owner: Redwood Finance / CorpFlux Procurement.

I've added items to the MAP spreadsheet for sign-off signatures. Attaching: CorpFlux_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP) and CorpFlux_SOW_draft.pdf (SOW).

Next steps: Kimberly and I can run a short onboarding session with your infra team next Wednesday (4/4) after you review the MAP. Does 11am PT work?

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com
Attachment: CorpFlux_MAP_v1.xlsx (XLSX), CorpFlux_SOW_draft.pdf (PDF)
From: Rajesh Menon <rajesh@corpflux.io>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Anna Lee <anna@corpflux.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-01T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: RE: CorpFlux GCP Private Offer — next steps

Sergio,

Quick clarifying questions from procurement:
- Will billing flow through the GCP private offer invoice (so we get one consolidated charge on our GCP bill) or will Redwood bill separately? We need this to map to our AP systems.
- Can you confirm the invoicing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly) and whether Redwood can support PO-based invoicing tied to the marketplace commitment ID?

Also, legal requests a redline-friendly SOW (Word preferred) and a short table summarizing SLAs / credits for missed targets.

Thanks,
Rajesh
Senior Procurement Manager, CorpFlux
procurement@corpflux.io
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Menon <procurement@corpflux.io>, Anna Lee <anna@corpflux.io>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-02T13:09:00-07:00
Subject: RE: CorpFlux GCP Private Offer — next steps

Rajesh — good questions. Short answers: 

- Billing path: Redwood supports billing via GCP Private Offer (charges appear on your consolidated GCP bill) OR Redwood can invoice directly if preferred. For marketplace private offers we default to marketplace invoicing to simplify PO reconciliation.
- Invoicing cadence: Monthly (Net 30). We can align invoice to the marketplace commitment ID and include a PO reference number.
- SOW format: We will send a redline-friendly Word SOW and an SLA table by tomorrow (4/3).

Action items we are pushing now:
- Kimberly: provision sandbox GCP project access and run initial smoke tests (due 4/10).
- Lauren: produce acceptance checklist with test scripts (due 4/17).
- Sergio: finalize MAP and share signed checklist template (due 4/4).

We can also include an escrow/holdback clause in the SOW if procurement needs a settlement trigger tied to acceptance gates.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lee <anna@corpflux.io>, Rajesh Menon <procurement@corpflux.io>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-03T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: CorpFlux GCP Private Offer — next steps

Anna / Rajesh — attaching the acceptance checklist and a short test-run playbook. Summary: 

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Functional: model responses pass 90% of validation prompts (per provided prompt-set).
- Performance: 95th perc latency < 320ms at nominal test load (sample load attached).
- Resilience: sustained 1k RPS smoke for 5 minutes without error spikes.

Test plan highlights (we will run together):
- Day 1: Connectivity and RBAC verification (owner: CorpFlux infra).
- Day 2: Throughput ramp and latency profiles (owner: Redwood / Lauren).
- Day 3: Acceptance sign-off meeting and signature capture (owners: Sergio + Rajesh).

Please find: acceptance_checklist.xlsx uploaded to the Drive link we shared earlier. If this looks good I'll schedule the sandbox kickoff for 4/10 and a joint acceptance run on 4/18.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com
Attachment: acceptance_checklist.xlsx (XLSX)
